title: Kabuliwala
director: claude-opus-5-5 (authored in Claude Code, same rules as scripts/audio/direct.ts)

cast.name: Narrator
cast.description: Warm adult storyteller, unhurried, gently amused, capable of deep tenderness

cast.name: Mini
cast.description: Five-year-old girl in Calcutta, a fearless, giggling chatterbox

cast.name: Rahamat
cast.description: Tall middle-aged Afghan fruit seller, deep voice, playful with children, later weary and heartbroken

cast.name: Mini's father
cast.description: Writer in his forties, Mini's father, kind but distracted and busy

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] Welcome to LitBridge, where stories cross languages. Today's story comes from Bengal. It was written in 1892 by Rabindranath Tagore... and it is called Kabuliwala.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [amused] The narrator is a writer in Calcutta, whose five-year-old daughter Mini cannot keep quiet for a minute.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One day she spots a tall Afghan in loose clothes and a turban, with a bag of raisins and almonds over his shoulder... and she calls out to him.

lines.speaker: mini
lines.text: [excited] Kabuliwala! Kabuliwala!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [chuckles] Then, terrified, she runs to hide.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Kabuliwala, Rahamat, keeps coming back. Before long the narrator finds the giant and the little girl sitting together, laughing at jokes only they understand.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He asks her what is in his bag.

lines.speaker: mini
lines.text: [giggles] An elephant!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He teases her about going to her father-in-law's house. And she, without missing a beat, asks him...

lines.speaker: mini
lines.text: [teasing] Are YOU going to your father-in-law's house?

lines.speaker: rahamat
lines.text: [mock anger] Ha! I would beat him! [laughs heartily]

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He shakes his fist at an imaginary father-in-law, and they both collapse in giggles.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [thoughtful] Mini's mother distrusts the stranger. But the narrator, who longs to travel and never does, enjoys his stories of the mountains.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [serious] One winter morning, Rahamat is led away by the police... his clothes stained with blood.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A man owed him money and denied it, and in the quarrel, Rahamat stabbed him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: As he passes, Mini calls out the old joke.

lines.speaker: mini
lines.text: [innocently] Are you going to your father-in-law's house?

lines.speaker: rahamat
lines.text: [bitter smile] Yes, little one. [short pause] That is exactly where I am going.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [softly] He is sentenced to years in prison.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [wistful] Time passes. Mini grows up... and forgets him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the morning of her wedding, as the musicians tune their instruments, Rahamat appears at the door. He has just been released. He has brought raisins for Mini, and he wants to see her.

lines.speaker: father
lines.text: [impatient] Not today, Rahamat. There is a wedding in the house. You will have to go.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [slowly] Rahamat turns back at the door... and unfolds a scrap of paper.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [tender] On it is the print of a tiny hand, pressed in soot. It belongs to his own daughter in Kabul, whom he left when she was Mini's age. He has carried it next to his heart all these years.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [moved] The narrator calls Mini, now in her bridal silk and sandal paste.

lines.speaker: rahamat
lines.text: [startled, softly] Little one... are you going to your father-in-law's house?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [heartbroken] She is no longer the little girl he knew. And Rahamat realises that his own daughter must have grown up too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] The narrator gives him money from the wedding budget, so that he can go home to her.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [long pause] Fewer lights are lit at the wedding that night... but the narrator thinks it is the brighter for it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [gently] Kabuliwala is a story about how love for a child crosses every border, of country, class, and language. Thank you for listening to LitBridge.
